text:
maya: Heads-up — thinking about adding a "simulator" button to the rollout UI so PMs/SEs can preview how an automatic fallback policy behaves on a slice of traffic. Want to kick around what outputs we should show in the console.
ryan: nice. what do we mean by 'preview'? replay historical traces or synthetic traffic?
maya: both ideally. start with a small replay from recent 1h window (anonymized) and let people tweak policy knobs (error thresholds, degrade mode, sampling rate) and see what would have happened.
tess: replay sounds good but privacy/PII concerns — must ensure we strip request payloads and only keep routing metadata + model decisions. logs should be hash-pseudonymized.
samir: UX question — do we show per-request decisions (i.e., which requests would have fallen back) or only aggregates? per-request is useful for debugging but noisy.
maya: propose pinned view: top-level aggregates (fallback rate, latency delta, cost delta) + expandable per-request table with redacted payload and a link to the trace id (opens trace view).
ryan: +1. Also show the reason codes for fallback (e.g., model-error, exceeding quota, KV cache miss, runtime OOM, latency SLO breach). That helps tune thresholds.
tess: add a timeline so you can see cascade effects (spike -> fallback surge -> cost spike). Those sequences help ops decide safe ramping.
samir: Implementation note — simulator will run against our policy engine sandbox. sample policy config we could expose in the UI: 

``` 
fallbackPolicy: {
  mode: "stealth" | "silent" | "graceful",
  trigger: { type: "error_rate", threshold: 0.05, window: "60s" },
  quota_behavior: "route-to-degraded" | "reject",
  sampling: { ratio: 0.1 }
}
```

samir: Need to decide what 'stealth' vs 'silent' means in docs. my take: stealth = redirect to variant but keep original response latency hints; silent = drop extra telemetry and don't surface fallback to end-user.
maya: we should avoid 'silent' defaults for customer-facing deployments. safer default: 'graceful' — fallback with explicit header/metadata so downstream can detect.
ryan: product ask: include expected unit cost delta (tokens, model unit price) computed from the replay — helps PM decide if fallback saved money.
tess: telemetry retention for sim runs? We can't keep full per-request preview longer than 24h for privacy. aggregates can be retained for 90d.
maya: +1. Also an 'audit export' that produces a CSV with decision timestamps, reason codes, model variants used, and a redacted request hash for compliance teams.
samir: ops/engineering implementation: the simulator will produce two streams — decisions (small) and sample payloads (opt-in). We'll gate sample payloads behind a checkbox and RBAC.
ryan: tiny UX nit: make the policy slider 'conservative -> aggressive' with numeric breakpoints, not free text. Also show rollback suggestion: e.g., if fallback rate > X and degradation causes >Y errors, suggest immediate rollback.
tess: what about multi-tenant noise? If a heavy tenant dominates the replay, we should surface tenant-level breakdown and allow filtering so policy tuning isn't skewed.
maya: yes — add tenant and route filters. Also let users pin a 'golden prompt set' for regression checks as part of the preview.
samir: sync question — should simulator call the real routing decision API or a local deterministic emulator? calling real API is more accurate but risks hitting infra quotas accidentally.
maya: prefer emulator that shares code with policy engine (same library), plus a 'dry-run' mode that actually calls the router with a flag to avoid affecting quotas.
ryan: we need clear language in the UI: "dry-run will not charge production quota" and show an estimated cost when toggled.
tess: security: audit logs for who ran the simulation, what policy they used, and ability to approve an exported audit pack. store approval events in immutable audit store.
deploy-bot: simulation job 2498765450 started by maya (dry-run=true) — 4k requests sampled, expected finish ~30s.
maya: ran the sim on the 1h window, top-line numbers: fallback rate 3.6%, avg latency uplift for fallback path +120ms, estimated cost delta -18% (due to cheaper base model). Paste sample CSV export link: https://redwood.internal/sim/2498765450/export.csv
ryan: quick look — can we annotate rows with 'reason confidence' (low/med/high) so users know whether a fallback happened due to noisy signal vs strong trigger?
samir: we can; the policy engine already has an internal score. expose a normalized confidence value 0-1 and a textual bucket.
tess: flag: some routes had cascading fallback oscillation in the sim when sampling ratio >0.5. we should show a recommended cooldown parameter to prevent oscillation.
maya: UX idea: simulate a staged rollout in the same UI — let you run 10% -> 25% -> 100% with simulated traffic and show cumulative impact.
ryan: love that. also allow 'compare' mode: two policies side-by-side on same replay.
samir: action items: 1) samir to draft API for simulator decisions + sample rows (spec). 2) tess to list privacy + retention constraints. 3) maya to mock the console UI and flows (simulate, export, approve). 4) ryan to collect PM asks for KPIs to display (cost, fallback rate, latency delta, error delta).
maya: thanks — will drop a Figma link in the channel later. can we include a small example of the audit CSV header that compliance wants?
ryan: yes, something like: 

```
run_id,timestamp,route,tenant_hash,request_hash,decision,reason_code,confidence,model_variant,latency_ms
```

maya: perfect. Also include a column 'trace_link' if available.
tess: last note — gating: only show per-request redacted rows to users with 'policy-sim.view.samples' permission. audits available to 'policy-sim.audit' role.
samir: will add RBAC hooks. timeline: aim for alpha in console two sprints from now.
maya: awesome — thanks all. follow-up: I'll post a short spec and the Figma tomorrow.
ryan: thanks, excited to try it.
deploy-bot: simulation job 2498765450 completed by maya — summary: 3.6% fallback, 12 routes affected, 2 tenants above 10% fallback.
